The test image shows a tomato leaf with distinctive dark brown/black ring-shaped and circular lesions (ring spots) covering most of the leaf surface. This pattern strongly suggests Tomato_Spotted_Wilt_Virus.

Let me view reference images across 8 different classes.

**Summary of observations:**

- **Test image**: Tomato leaf with multiple dark brownish-black circular ring spots showing concentric ring (bullseye) patterns spread across the leaf — classic ring spot symptom.

- **TSWV references**: Bugwood_137 clearly shows ring/concentric spot pattern (on pepper fruit); Bugwood_10 shows spots on leaf — consistent with TSWV ring spot symptoms.
- **Early_Blight**: Shows brown/necrotic patches or browning edges — no ring spots.
- **CMV**: Shows leaf curling/mosaic distortion — no match.
- **Bacterial_Speck**: Shows tiny specks on fruit — no match.
- **Septoria Leaf Blotch**: Shows small circular spots with yellow halos on yellowing leaf — not the dark concentric rings pattern.

The dark concentric ring spots spread across a green tomato leaf are a hallmark symptom of Tomato Spotted Wilt Virus (TSWV), caused by *Tospovirus*. No other candidate class produces this pattern.
